title: Processes and state
summary: A process is a running program with its own execution state. A process can run, be ready to run, or block while waiting for an event.
claims: A process state describes whether it can currently use the CPU.

misconceptions.text: Every ready process executes at once.

title: Creating a child with fork
summary: fork creates a child process. After a successful call, both parent and child continue from the return point, with different return values.
claims: The child receives zero from fork; the parent receives the child PID.
Creating a child does not determine which process runs next.

misconceptions.text: The child always runs before the parent.

title: Waiting for a child
summary: wait or waitpid lets a parent block until a child changes state and then collect its termination status. It orders the parent's post-wait work after that child's exit.
claims: A wait in the parent can prevent its completion message from appearing before the child's exit.
A wait call in the child does not block the parent.

misconceptions.text: wait fixes the order of every print statement in both processes.
Calling wait in the child makes the parent wait.

title: Replacing a program with exec
summary: A successful exec replaces the current process image. It does not create another process, and execution does not continue after the call.
claims: The process ID remains the same across a successful exec.
Code after exec runs only when exec fails.
